slides.headline: October 23, 2022: India's heaviest rocket flew its first paying customer.
ISRO's LVM3 carried 36 OneWeb satellites into orbit from Sriharikota
slides.body: It was the first fully commercial launch of LVM3 - India's heaviest-lift rocket, normally reserved for government missions - arranged through NewSpace India Limited, ISRO's commercial arm.

slides.headline: All 36 satellites separated successfully, bringing OneWeb's constellation to 462 satellites.
slides.body: The mission marked India's entry into the global commercial launch services market - a rocket built for the country's own missions now earning revenue by flying someone else's payload.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat needs a space program that earns revenue, not just one that explores.
slides.body: Turning India's heaviest rocket into a commercial product - available to any customer, not just the government - showed a path for the space program to fund itself.
